result.verdict: From a code-execution safety standpoint, PR #12 is fit to merge. The new .github/workflows/research.yml triggers only on pull_request, push to main and workflow_dispatch, with no pull_request_target. It sets `permissions: contents: read`, uses no secrets and pins actions the same way as the other workflows (checkout@v7, setup-python@v7, upload-artifact@v4, all watched by dependabot). It installs only numpy==2.3.5, as other workflows already do. It runs `sudo sysctl vm.mmap_rnd_bits=28` on a throwaway runner for TSan, which is the standard workaround. Its one network step (`tools/bench_huf4.py --sample-k3`) reads four 1 MiB ranges from huggingface.co. Those reads are pinned to a commit revision, SHA-256 checked, and go through the existing `remote_model.read_range`, which insists on HTTP 206, checks Content-Range and Content-Encoding, and caps the read length. The `bench_lossless` job in offline-storage.yml already makes the same kind of request. The new Python tools start processes with list arguments and no shell, and `routing_probe` loads NPZ files with `allow_pickle=False`. The new cgroup test uses `sudo -n systemd-run` only when K3_CGROUP_TEST=1, the same pattern the existing lm-head cgroup test uses. Nothing is obfuscated. The PR changes no Makefile, CMake or pip rules. In a /tmp copy, `make test`, the ASan/UBSan and TSan row-lifetime builds, the routing and lookahead unittests, and the synthetic huf4 and io_uring benchmarks all passed. After `make test` I found no new /tmp entry of this PR's, and the successful io_uring run cleaned up after itself. I could not run the pinned-sample HuggingFace download because the sandbox proxy returns 403. I found two low-severity items and nothing that blocks the merge. Both are unchanged at the final head origin/claude/predictive-prefetch-research-cqti31, where research.yml and bench_uring.c are the same as in this PR.

findings.title: io_uring benchmark leaves a partly written file of up to 64 MiB in /tmp when setup fails
findings.detail: main() creates its file with a fixed path, mkstemp("/tmp/k3-uring-XXXXXX"), so TMPDIR is ignored. It unlinks the file only at line 134, after the 64 MiB write and fsync. The early returns before that point skip the unlink and leave the partial file behind: posix_memalign failure (line 127), a short write (line 130) or fsync failure (line 132). The most likely trigger is a full or quota-limited /tmp, which is exactly when a leftover file hurts most. The fix is to call unlink(path) right after mkstemp; the file stays usable through fd until it is reopened, or the code can reopen through /proc/self/fd, or unlink on every error path. The file is identical at the final stack head.
findings.evidence: In a /tmp copy of the PR tree I built it with the CI command (cc -O3 -std=gnu99 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -fopenmp benchmarks/bench_uring.c) and ran `bash -c "trap '' XFSZ; ulimit -f 2048; ./bench-uring"`. It exited with rc=2 and left /tmp/k3-uring-9pQ1ix (2097152 bytes, mode 0600) behind; I deleted it afterwards. A normal run with no size limit exited 0 and left nothing behind.

findings.title: Research workflow runs on every PR with a network download and no job timeouts
findings.detail: `on: pull_request` has no paths filter, so all five jobs run on every PR, including docs-only ones. That includes the decoder job on ubuntu-latest and macos-14, whose step at line 54 fetches pinned ranges from huggingface.co. None of the jobs sets timeout-minutes, so GitHub's 360-minute default applies. Most of the repo's workflows set timeouts: kda, offline-storage, remote-storage, scale-plane, mla-variants and trunk-dictionary each have at least one. ci.yml sets none. This is not a security hole: the token is read-only, no secrets are used and the downloads are SHA-verified. But any outage or rate limit at HuggingFace will fail CI on unrelated PRs, and a hung job would hold a runner for up to 6 hours. A paths filter and short timeout-minutes would fix both. The workflow is unchanged at the final stack head.
findings.evidence: research.yml lines 2-6 show the triggers with no paths filter. A grep of timeout-minutes finds 0 in research.yml at both the PR head and the final head, compared with 1-5 in the other workflows. Running `tools/bench_huf4.py --sample-k3` in the sandbox failed immediately with `URLError: Tunnel connection failed: 403 Forbidden` (the proxy blocks huggingface.co). That shows the step fails hard whenever the host cannot be reached, though it does not show that the host is unreliable on GitHub runners.

findings.title: bench_uring leaves a partly written file of up to 64 MiB in /tmp when it fails early
findings.detail: main() creates /tmp/k3-uring-XXXXXX with mkstemp (line 123-124). The /tmp path is hard-coded and TMPDIR is ignored. It then writes 64 x 1 MiB blocks and fsyncs. It unlinks the file only after closing and reopening it with O_DIRECT (line 134). The early `return 2` paths skip the unlink: posix_memalign failure (127), a short or failed write (130) and fsync failure (132). A failure caused by ENOSPC on a small tmpfs /tmp, RLIMIT_FSIZE or EIO therefore leaves the partial file behind, just when space is already short. A SIGINT during the write phase leaves it too. The normal path cleans up. Possible fixes: unlink on each error path; or set O_DIRECT on the existing descriptor with fcntl(F_SETFL), which works on Linux, and unlink right after mkstemp. The file is unchanged at the final stack head.

findings.title: research.yml sets no timeout-minutes on any of its jobs

result.verdict: From a correctness standpoint PR #12 is fit to merge, though the rows unit test should be strengthened and the new refusals should print messages. The core of the PR is `--trunk-rows`: two buffers with one outstanding job, a wait before every submit and before every bind, and row-tiled calls to the unchanged per-row kernels. It is exact and race-free in everything I ran. `make test` passes. The 93-layer `-DK3_TEST_ROWS_ONLY` build passes under ASan/UBSan. CLI builds with ThreadSanitizer and with ASan/UBSan are clean in rows mode (the only ASan reports are leaks from the config reader, which predate this PR). I ran about 100 successful comparisons of `--trunk-rows` against the ring trunk on the tiny model: plain and compressed trunks; full recompute, `--incremental`, `--kv-latent`, `--spec` 2/3/4, `--ultra-low-memory`, `--stream-lm-head`, `--reread-prompt`, `--layers 5` and `--expert-pipeline`; 1 and 4 threads; and the smallest budget that opens, where each tile holds 16 rows. Generated IDs and dumped logits were bit-identical in every case. Truncating `trunk.bin` inside a matrix gives the sticky error 'trunk row read failed at layer 6; refusing partial output', with no JSON written. The JSON-tree free and the OpenMP reduction fix are correct. A fuzz run of 400 random inputs with code lengths 1 to 12 found no decode errors in the four-stream decoder, and the lookahead cost arithmetic checks out. The remaining problems are test strength, diagnostics and tool contracts; none changes emitted tokens or logits. The rows exactness test in `test_trunk.c` cannot fail when row tiles are misplaced; only the Linux-only, torch-based CLI test catches that. The new `trunk.json` checks refuse silently, and one of them rejects a setup that main ran. The rows-mode report claims 100% of reads overlapped compute. The memory plan charges the whole `--trunk-gb`. `routing_probe` rejects multiple continuations of one prompt group. All five are still present at the final head `origin/claude/predictive-prefetch-research-cqti31`.

findings.title: Row-tile exactness checks cannot fail: every fixture tensor is one repeated byte
findings.detail:
`gen_layer_run` fills each tensor with a single repeated marker byte (`fill_marker`). Every row of a matrix is therefore identical, and every output of `k3_mmw` has the same value. `test_rows` compares `--trunk-rows` output with the whole-layer trunk using `memcmp`, so it passes for any tile-offset, row-order or O_DIRECT-prefix error that stays inside the tensor.

In the default `make test` build (buffers of 12288 bytes, 4096-byte payload, largest matrix 512 bytes) every matrix is a single tile, so the double-buffered path is not exercised at all. The `-DK3_TEST_ROWS_ONLY` 93-layer build does use multiple tiles (the research.yml 'Row pipeline lifetimes' job, run under TSan and ASan), but it still cannot detect a misplaced tile. `docs/notes/research-results.md` nevertheless cites these tests as covering 'unaligned row starts, ragged row/tile tails'.

The only guard is `tests/test_offline_cli.py`, which runs only on Linux CI with torch. The weakness is still present at the final head: the fixture is unchanged, and the new 'batched positions, one pass' check also passes under the same mutation.

Fix: fill tensors with position-dependent bytes, for example a hash of layer, tensor and byte index.
findings.evidence:
Mutation in `rows_apply`: `rows_submit(r, 1 - slot, m->off, ...)` and `off = m->off`, so every tile after the first re-reads tile 0.
- 93-layer `-DK3_TEST_ROWS_ONLY` ASan build: all 5 'rows:' checks PASS, 'TRUNK TESTS PASSED'.
- Default `make test` build of `test_trunk`: PASS.
- Same mutation in the final head's `rows_run`: all 6 rows checks PASS, including 'rows: batched positions, one pass'.
- `test_offline_cli.py -k trunk_rows` with the mutated engine: FAILED (failures=6), `generated_ids` [83, 31] != [28, 61].

findings.title: New trunk.json checks refuse with no message; the layer-count check rejects a setup main ran
findings.detail:
`trunk_open`'s new checks all `goto bad` without printing anything: the layer count against `c->n_layers`, `json_size` for `file_off`/`nbytes`/`off`/`nbytes`, tensor bounds, and F32/BF16 offset alignment. The CLI then only does `if (rc != 0) return 1;`, so the user gets exit code 1 with empty stderr.

The `tr->n_layers > c->n_layers` rejection is only needed to bound `rows_open`'s per-layer metadata loop, but it also applies to the default ring mode. It turns a combination that main accepted into a silent failure. The CLI's own `trunk.n_layers < NL` check shows that trunks with more layers than needed were meant to be accepted. Still present at the final head (line 387).

Tiny model with a 12-layer `--config` over the 13-layer trunk, `--trunk-gb 0.001`:

- PR head: rc=1, 0 bytes of stderr.
- Final head: rc=1, 0 bytes of stderr.

A `trunk.json` with one F32 tensor's `off` increased by 2: PR head rc=1, 0 bytes of stderr.

findings.title: Rows-mode trunk report claims 100% of reads overlapped compute
findings.detail:
The rows branch of `k3_trunk_bind` returns before `t_bind0`, `k3_trunk_binds` and `k3_trunk_bind_wall` are updated. Meanwhile `rows_read` adds all device time to `load_seconds`, including two kinds of read that are not overlapped:
- the synchronous copies of the current layer's vectors, which the main thread does inside bind (at released dimensions this includes the 25.7 MB fp32 router gate on every MoE layer);
- the first tile of every matrix, which `rows_apply` waits for immediately.

`k3_trunk_report` then computes overlapped = `load_seconds` - 0 and prints that all device time overlapped compute on the reader thread, over 0 binds. The research note tells users to inspect these counters to judge the rows tradeoff. Still present at the final head.
findings.evidence: PR head, `k3 fx/selective --ids 3,7,11 --gen 2 --trunk fx/trunk --trunk-gb 0.00005 --trunk-rows` prints: 'bind wall 0.00 s over 0 binds; read 0.20 + widen 0.00 = 0.20 s of device work, of which 0.20 s (100%) overlapped compute on the reader thread'. The final head prints the same with 0.09 s.

findings.title: --trunk-rows memory plan charges the whole --trunk-gb, and the implicit 16 GB default is accepted
findings.detail:
The pre-allocation plan and `memory_plan_bytes` charge `trunk_gb*1e9` for the trunk even in rows mode. Rows mode allocates at most 2 x (8 MiB + 8 KiB) plus the vector arena (43.3 MB at released dimensions).

The guard at line 890 rejects only `auto`. The error text and the research note both say an explicit `--trunk-gb` is required, but omitting it silently uses the 16 GB default. The CLI then refuses to start on a 16 GB machine for a mode that needs tens of MB. Still present at the final head.
findings.evidence: PR head, `k3 fx/selective --ids 3,7,11 --trunk fx/trunk --trunk-rows` (no `--trunk-gb`): 'REFUSING TO START: this needs 16.00 GB and the machine has 16.14 GB available'. The final head gives the same refusal with 15.93 GB available. With `--trunk-gb 0.00005` the same run opens 'two 16384-byte buffers + 10864-byte current-layer vectors'.

findings.title: routing_probe rejects multiple continuations of one prompt group, contrary to its documented split contract
findings.detail:
The docstring defines `prompt[]` as group IDs and says the split is by original prompt 'including all its trajectories'. `predictive-prefetch-gates.md` also requires all continuations of one original prompt to stay in one split. But the uniqueness key is (prompt, position, layer), so two decode continuations of the same prompt at the same generated positions are refused as duplicates.

The only workaround, a separate ID per trajectory, removes the tool's ability to keep continuations of one prompt in the same split, which is the leakage guard. The file is unchanged at the final head.

result.verdict: From the code-execution safety lens, PR #13 is fit to merge. The new trunk-dictionary.yml runs only on pull_request (path-filtered) and workflow_dispatch, never pull_request_target or workflow_run, and nothing in the repo uses either. It sets permissions to contents: read, uses persist-credentials: false on every checkout, uses no secrets, and puts no untrusted event text into shell. The histogram artifact is passed between jobs within one run only (the log shows run-id pinned to the current run). The two new tools call the caller-supplied binary with a list-form subprocess, keep scratch files in a private TemporaryDirectory, and write only --out and GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY. They download exactly eight 1 MiB ranges from a hard-coded huggingface.co URL. The revision must be a 40-hex SHA and shard names must match a strict pattern. read_range rejects responses that are not 206, have the wrong range, are compressed or are the wrong length, and each range's SHA-256 is checked before its bytes are used (trunk_dictionary_gate.py:155-158, bench_fixed_dictionary.py:63-67). Nothing is added to make, make test, CMake/ctest or pip install. Checks I ran locally: the new unittests pass with socket connects blocked and file opens logged (no network, no writes). The sanitizer C test exits 0, and the deliberate trip-asan and trip-ubsan controls exit 86 and 87 with the expected messages; they run only with those explicit arguments. The driver's negative controls return a clean 1. The tools' GITHUB_ACTIONS checks are policy markers, not a security boundary, and bypassing them only allows the same hash-checked 8 MiB fetch. I could not run the real-range fetch because this sandbox's proxy blocks huggingface.co. The only item is low-severity hygiene: actions are referenced by mutable tags, and the v4 artifact actions target the deprecated Node 20. The network, integrity and subprocess code is unchanged at the final head. The final head also adds a families job and a contention job (which runs brew install libomp); those belong to #14's review.

It also introduces actions/download-artifact@v4 (lines 80, 136), the repo's first use of that action. All are movable major-version tags, not commit SHAs. result.verdict: Fit to merge from a correctness lens. The PR adds research and benchmark code only. It changes nothing in the engine, the Makefile or CMake, so no engine exactness contract is affected, and neither build picks up the new C files. The FD4B codec is correct and memory-safe on the scalar, SSSE3 and NEON paths. I ran a differential fuzz: 70k random streams plus corrupted copies, in exact-size heap buffers, under gcc ASan+UBSan on x86 and qemu for aarch64. It found no sanitizer reports and no scalar/native disagreements. The PR's C test, both Python suites, ruff 0.16.3 and compileall all pass locally. The gate arithmetic uses integer counts. Doc figures (pooled escapes 1,902; per-range r and coverage) match CI run 35498176696. That run is green at head 9f0c07f for histogram, exactness and rate on ubuntu and macos-14, and the macOS rate report shows PASS. The problems I found are test-strength gaps only; none blocks merge. First, the escape-underflow test cannot detect removal of the decoders' out-of-bounds guards; this is fixed at the final head. Second, the duplicate-range check and the duplicate-table check are untested; both gaps are still present at the final head.

findings.title: Escape-underflow test cannot detect removal of the escape-stream bounds guards (out-of-bounds read)
findings.detail: The underflow case sets `copy[32] |= 15` on a stream of about 6.2 KB held in `uint8_t copy[17001]`, a stack array (line 55). `v.escape` = copy+length therefore still points inside the array. The in-loop guard `if (e == v->escapes) return -1;` sits in all four decode loops (fixed_dictionary.h lines 69 scalar, 102 SSSE3, 121 NEON, 132 tail). If it is deleted, the decoder reads escape[0] past the end of the stream without ASan noticing, and the trailing `e == v->escapes` check still returns -1, so the CHECK passes. No other CI step covers this. bench_fixed_dictionary.c read_file allocates length+1, which hides a one-byte over-read, and the Python negative controls never corrupt escape counts. The effect is that a regression in this memory-safety guard would ship with green CI. The guards themselves are currently correct (the fuzz found no errors). Final head: fixed. Underflow and surplus now go through refused(), which uses exact-size heap_copy() buffers, and the same mutants fail there.
findings.evidence: Mutation runs at PR head 9f0c07f (scratch copies in /tmp/claude-0/rv13m, run_mut.sh): I deleted each of the four guards in turn. `test_fixed_dictionary` still printed PASS with exit 0 in three builds: gcc -O1 -fsanitize=address,undefined -mssse3; the same without -mssse3 (scalar); and aarch64 under qemu, including a variant with a guard-page malloc. I then put the same corrupted stream in an exact-size heap buffer (/tmp/claude-0/rv13m/underflow_harness.c). The SSSE3 and scalar mutants report `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow ... READ of size 1 ... in fwd_decode_native fixed_dictionary.h:103` (exit 86); the original returns -1 cleanly. At final head cb4ab38 the same mutants make the test exit 86 on x86 ASan, and the NEON mutants SIGSEGV with a guard-page heap under qemu.

The check that matters is therefore untested: a manifest where one dense row is replaced by a copy of another still has 8 rows, scores one range twice and silently drops one. findings.title: Duplicate-table-entry case passes whether or not fwd_parse rejects duplicates
findings.detail: `copy[17] = copy[16]` sets table[1] to table[0]'s value. The no-escape stream uses code 1, so the decoded bytes differ and `exact()` fails on memcmp even when fwd_parse accepts the table. The distinctness loop in fwd_parse (benchmarks/fixed_dictionary.h:36-38) is therefore never exercised: deleting it leaves the suite green. A duplicate entry cannot cause an unsafe access, so the impact is limited to an unverified format-validation check. To make the case discriminating, duplicate a slot the data never uses, or assert on fwd_parse directly. Still present at the final head: same test, check at fixed_dictionary.h:55-57.

result.verdict: Fit to merge from a code-execution-safety standpoint. Nothing blocks it. Every workflow keeps `permissions: contents: read` and triggers only on pull_request, push or workflow_dispatch (never pull_request_target). No secrets are referenced, and the PR adds no third-party actions: the new steps use first-party actions/* at the same tag pins the repo already uses, and msys2/setup-msys2@v2 is unchanged. No untrusted `${{ }}` values are interpolated into run: scripts. Most new jobs set persist-credentials: false; the new avx512-kernels job follows ci.yml's existing default, and its token is read-only. The Windows fix installs the official MSYS2 package mingw-w64-x86_64-libgomp, and that job passed on the head. The only new network access is to huggingface.co, from trunk_family_gate.py. It runs only in CI, pins the revision to a validated 40-hex commit, and reuses the unchanged remote_model.py helpers (HTTPS, 64 MiB caps, header validation). I ran `make test` at the head under strace: no sockets, only the compiler toolchain and the repo's own test binaries were executed, and all writes stayed in-tree or in /tmp (the temp dirs are removed afterwards). The five new or changed Python test modules also pass with no sockets. spec_replay.py only reads local package directories and the repo's git history (git is called with a plain argument list, no shell) and writes only its --work and --out paths; the committed output JSON holds aggregate numbers only. bench_mla's popen runs a fixed macOS `sysctl` command. The 58-commit history contains no credentials, no stray files and no binary blobs. Two low-severity items remain: an unsafe copy-paste reproduce snippet in the docs, and path triggers that tie routine kernel and Makefile PRs to Hugging Face downloads and long timing jobs. Both are still present at the final head, origin/claude/predictive-prefetch-research-cqti31.

findings.title: Reproduce snippet uses unquoted `rm -rf $D`, and its second block relies on `$D` from the first
findings.detail: The 'Reproduce' block starts with `D=/path/to/kern-timing; rm -rf $D; mkdir -p $D/base && ...`. `$D` is unquoted and has no guard. If a reader edits D to a path containing a space, rm word-splits it and deletes two unintended paths, one outside the chosen directory and one relative to the repo root the snippet runs from. The router block at lines 199-213 uses `$D` again (`-o $D/router_*`, `tee $D/router.log`) but never sets it. Pasted into a fresh shell, it compiles binaries and writes the log at the filesystem root, which succeeds when run as root, as is common in containers. This is documentation only; nothing in make or CI runs it. Still present at the final head (the head of #14). Suggested fix: `D=$(mktemp -d)`, `rm -rf -- "${D:?}"`, quote every `$D`, and either set D in the router block or merge the two blocks.

With D unset (`env -u D bash`) it printed `cc ... -o /router_old_native -lm` (and the same for the other three binaries) and `WOULD WRITE: /router.log`.

As a result, any ordinary kernel or header PR now makes unauthenticated requests to huggingface.co. The `histogram` job fetches eight 1 MiB ranges. result.verdict: Fit to merge from a correctness lens. I found no logic, exactness, memory-safety or build bug in the source, CI, Makefile/CMake or tools changes, and nothing blocks the #12 → #13 → #14 merge. Evidence I ran: `make test` passes on the native AVX-512 build, AVX2 (`-mavx2 -mfma`), plain scalar x86, clang AVX2 and CMake/ctest. Under qemu, GCC aarch64 NEON builds of test_ops, test_matmul_exact, test_kda_exact and k3_model all pass, including GATE 4. A standalone harness wrote the outputs of the bf16 and f32 single-position and batched kernels (T=1..17, cancelling data and NaN/sNaN inputs) plus the router. Its files were byte-identical across AVX-512, AVX512F-only, AVX2, scalar, NEON, gcc and clang, and at 1, 3 and 4 threads. MXFP4 on AVX-512 matches AVX2; scalar and NEON differ only in the sign of NaN outputs, which the NaN rule exempts. Forcing K3_MM_TB to 1, 2, 4 or 8 passes. When I broke the batched tile's reduction tree or removed its NaN canonicalisation, test_ops failed, so that gate has teeth. test_offline_cli passes on both the optimised and the ASan/UBSan engine. 176 randomised serial-vs-speculative CLI runs (n-gram and draft trunk, --kv-latent, --trunk-rows, stop ids, --save-state and --load-state) gave identical ids, per-token logits and saved-state bytes, with forward_sweeps equal to decode_steps. Resident, ultra, rows, incremental and kv-latent modes give identical logits for every token. With an expert that fails to load, the prefill MoE output matches per-token k3_moe under ASan. test_mla_variants and the KDA, model and trunk tests are clean under ASan/UBSan. The WIP commits in the history build and pass. CI is green on the PR head, including Windows (libgomp fix) and the AVX-512 job, which reported "RAN". The two findings are both low severity and still present at the final head origin/claude/predictive-prefetch-research-cqti31.

findings.title: Contention and MLA timings were measured on the kernels this PR replaces, and the shipped kernel changes the conclusions
findings.detail: The contention measurements (head 516f010, per the reports' execution.head_sha) and the MLA timings (commit 475a7a8, 'isa':'AVX2' in the jsonl) both predate the kernel commits 4518417 and 3612040. The docs still present them as the engine's k3_matmul_bf16 (CHANGELOG.md:84-86 and 66-71, STATUS.md:111, research-results.md:339, mla-variants.md 'what --kv-latent pays ... today: 24 minutes'). I rebuilt bench_decode_contention against both kernel versions on the same VM type and ran them interleaved; the old kernel reproduces the committed tables closely. With the shipped kernel, three conclusions change. (1) On 2 threads the matmul is no longer the limiting stage: B=6 at the median goes from about 0.88 (matmul-limited, fail) to 1.11-1.13 (decode-limited, pass). The note's explanation 'the decoder's core leaves the matmul one thread at about 5.1 GB/s' describes the old kernel. (2) On 4 threads the worst case at B=5 falls from about 1.15 to 1.06 on a quiet run, and to 0.97-1.00 under background load. B=4 is no longer the full 1/r. (3) The resident slowdown rises from the 2.08-3.62 quoted to 4.4-6.2 on 4 threads; the hosted x86 leg on cb4ab38 shows 5.73-6.12. For MLA, the kv_b unit cost falls from 4.15-4.19 ms to 2.38-2.39 ms on 1 thread and from 0.78 ms to 0.51-0.63 ms on 4 threads. So the latent-path absolute times, the L1-vs-E+ ratios and the '24 minutes' figure are overstated for the shipped engine. PR #14 already re-timed the batched matmul for exactly this reason (research-results 'measured batching against a kernel this branch no longer ships') but did not do the same here. result.verdict: From the code-safety lens PR #11 is safe to merge, but it should be closed as superseded rather than merged. It is one signed commit (34a8d6d) that changes only CHANGELOG.md, docs/STATUS.md and a new docs/notes/research-queue.md. All three are plain 100644 files, pure ASCII with no control or bidi characters. It changes no workflow, script, Makefile, CMake or pyproject file, adds no external URLs, and asks no one to run any command. Nothing in make, make test, pip install or CI reads these three files: CMake and CI read README.md and docs/measurements/*.json, which #11 does not touch. Every relative link resolves, and all 20 CI checks passed on its head. The shelved Huffman files it points contributors to are unchanged by #11 and work locally only (read argv[1], write argv[2], no network or subprocess). However, its only commit is already the first commit of #12, and so of #13 and #14; #12's description says so. Merging the stack with the repo's usual two-parent merge commits brings 34a8d6d into main, and GitHub should then mark #11 merged. Merging #11 first is redundant: the final tree comes out identical. Squash or rebase merges, of #11 or of the stack, conflict in all three files. Its wording is also stale: the final head rewrote both docs and explicitly retracts several of its claims. Recommend: close #11 as superseded by #12 rather than keep it open as the "rolling PR" its description says an automated loop will push to.
